body.p: Remarks

As stated above, Applicant appreciates the Examiner's thorough examination of the subject application and requests reexamination and reconsideration of the subject application in view of the preceding amendments and the following remarks.

As of the subject action, claims 1-16 and 19-30 were pending in the subject application, of which claims 1, 19, and 27 are independent claims. With this Response, Applicant has amended claims 1, 19, and 27 and has cancelled claim 7. Applicant respectfully submits that no new matter is believed to have been entered as a result of this Response. All objections and rejections are respectfully traversed.

Claims 1-3, 5, 12-20, 22, 27, and 29 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Edinger et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,346,160, hereinafter referred to as "Edinger") in view of either Correll et al. (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0381670, hereinafter referred to as "Correll") or Crawley (U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0079532, hereinafter referred to as "Crawley"). Claims 4, 6-11, 21, 23-26, 28, and 30 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Edinger in view of Correll or Crawley as applied to claims 1, 19, and 27 above, and further in view of Gilbertson et al. (U.S. Patent No. 9,827,678, hereinafter referred to as "Gilbertson"). Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Without conceding the rejection and in an effort to accelerate prosecution of the subject application, Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 19, and 27. Representative independent claim 1 is recited below for convenience:
1. (Currently Amended) A detachable, self-contained robotic arm
system comprising:
a mounting subsystem configured to releasably engage an operating platform, wherein the operating platform is an autonomous
mobile base;

a robotic arm subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem; a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the mounting subsystem, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate

p.u: the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system
a second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem, wherein the second machine vision system is configured to
of areas proximate the robotic arm subsystem

body.p: a control subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem and configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem;
and
a connectivity subsystem configured to detachably couple the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system to one or more external
systems.
Support for these amendments may be found in at least dependent claim 7 and paragraphs [0033]-[0034] of the subject application as published, which are reproduced below for convenience.

[0033] To properly position machine vision system 64 and/or audio system 66 with respect to detachable, self-contained robotic arm system 10, machine vision system 64 and/or audio system 66 may be mounted on mast assembly 68 coupled (i.e., directly or indirectly) to mounting subsystem 12. Through the use of mast assembly 68, an elevated point of view may be achieved with respect to the moving parts of detachable, self-contained robotic arm system 10, thus providing situational awareness to avoid collision and/or permit safe operation by humans within the reachable proximity of the moving parts of detachable, self-contained
robotic arm system 10 and/or its payload.
[0034] Machine vision system 64 may be configured to include multiple / additional machine vision systems (e.g., multiple / additional cameras).

Accordingly, one or more additional cameras may be positioned along robotic arm subsystem 26. For example, these additional cameras may be mounted on robotic arm subsystem 26 and may provide visual target identification for object pick-up and/or positioning, as well as proximate object detection to allow for safe operation of robotic arm subsystem 26 near moving and stationary objects. An example of such a machine vision system may include but is not limited to the
Intel® RealSenseTM D435 depth camera.
(See, subject application as filed, paragraphs [0033]-[0034]).

Applicant respectfully submits that the combination of Edinger, Correll, Crawley, and/or Gilbertson fails to teach, disclose, or even suggest "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the mounting subsystem, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system"; "a second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem, wherein the second machine vision system is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm subsystem"; and "a control subsystem coupled to
the mounting subsystem and configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem."

For example, in rejecting dependent claim 7, the subject action states "Gilbertson teaches a robot arm having a machine vision system to visually monitor areas proximate the robotic arm. For example, see paragraph spanning columns 11 and 12." See, subject action, p. 5. Col. 11, 1.
55 - col. 12, 1. 16 of Gilbertson is reproduced below for convenience.

The sensor(s) 112 may provide sensor data to the processor(s) 102 (perhaps by way of data 107) to allow for interaction of the robotic system 100 with its environment, as well as monitoring of the operation of the robotic system 100.

The sensor data may be used in evaluation of various factors for activation, movement, and deactivation of mechanical components 110 and electrical components 116 by control system 118. For example, the sensor(s) 112 may capture data corresponding to the terrain of the environment, the layout of the environment (e.g., the floor plan of the house, apartment, condominium, business residence, etc.), the surface geometry of the environment (e.g., stairs, inclines, etc.), location of nearby objects, and/or identity of nearby objects, which may assist with environment recognition and navigation. In an example configuration, sensor(s) 112 may include RADAR (e.g., for long-range object detection, distance determination, and/or speed determination), LIDAR (e.g., for short-range object detection, distance determination, and/or speed determination), SONAR (e.g., for underwater object detection, distance determination, and/or speed determination), VICON® (e.g., for motion capture), one or more cameras (e.g., stereoscopic cameras for 3D vision), a global positioning system (GPS) transceiver, and/or other sensors for capturing information of the environment in which the robotic system 100 is operating. The sensor(s) 112 may monitor the environment in real time, and detect obstacles, elements of the terrain, weather conditions,
temperature, and/or other aspects of the environment.
(See, Gilbertson, col. 11, 1. 55 - col. 12, 1. 16; emphasis added).

As can be seen from at least the above-cited portions of Gilbertson, the combination of Edinger, Correll, Crawley, and/or Gilbertson is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the mounting subsystem or a second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem. As such, Applicants respectfully submit that the combination of Edinger is not understood to teach, disclose, or suggest Applicant's claimed "a first machine vision subsystem mounted on a mast assembly coupled to the mounting subsystem, wherein the first machine vision subsystem is

configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the detachable, self-contained robotic arm system"; "a second machine vision subsystem mounted on the robotic arm subsystem, wherein the second machine vision system is configured to enable visually monitoring of areas proximate the robotic arm subsystem"; and "a control subsystem coupled to the mounting subsystem and configured to effectuate movement of the robotic arm assembly using the first machine vision subsystem and the second machine vision subsystem."

Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-6, 8-16, and 19-30 under § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Edinger, Correll, Crawley, and/or Gilbertson be withdrawn.

In this response, Applicant has amended various claims and/or asserted arguments in this application to facilitate expeditious prosecution of the application. Applicant is not conceding that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to the instant action, and/or having interpretations other than presented herein are unpatentable over the art cited by the Examiner. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue claims in one or more continuing applications, including claims capturing the subject matter encompassed by any claims prior to this response, claims having different interpretations than presented in this response, and additional claims.

In consideration of the amendments and foregoing discussion, Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is in condition for allowance. While Applicant respectfully asserts that the subject application is now in condition for allowance, the Examiner is invited to telephone Applicant's representative (617-854-1420) to facilitate prosecution of this application. Please apply any charges or credits to the above-noted deposit account.
